description: Dream11 Fantasy Point System & Cricket Rules Knowledge Base for CricIQ AI Assistant

dream11_scoring.description: Official Dream11 fantasy point system for IPL and other cricket formats

batting.description: Points awarded to batsmen based on performance

points.rule: 1 point per run scored
1 additional point for hitting a four (total 2 points for a four)
2 additional points for hitting a six (total 3 points per six)
1 point bonus when a batsman scores 30 or more runs
2 point bonus when a batsman scores 50 or more runs
4 point bonus when a batsman scores 100 or more runs
+2 points for batsmen who face at least 50 balls and maintain strike rate above 120
-2 points for batsmen who face at least 50 balls and have strike rate below 60

bowling.description: Points awarded to bowlers based on performance

points.rule: 25 points per wicket
+4 additional points for wickets taken via caught, bowled, LBW, or stumped (total 29 points)
+6 additional points for wickets taken via caught and bowled by the bowler (total 31 points)
4 point bonus when a bowler takes 3 or more wickets in an innings
8 point bonus when a bowler takes 4 or more wickets in an innings
12 point bonus when a bowler takes 5 or more wickets in an innings
2 points per maiden over bowled
+2 points for bowlers with economy rate below 6 (minimum 10 overs bowled)
+1 point for bowlers with economy rate between 6 and 8 (minimum 10 overs bowled)
-2 points for bowlers with economy rate above 10 (minimum 10 overs bowled)
6 points per catch
12 points for a stumping (includes wicket points)
12 points for a direct hit run-out
6 points for assisting in a run-out
-2 points for every wicket lost while bowling (does not apply to run-outs)
-6 points if a fielder causes a run-out of their own team's batsman through error
No penalty for batsmen who remain not out

cricket_rules.description: Common cricket rules and concepts explained simply

dls_method.name: Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) Method
dls_method.explanation: A mathematical formula used to calculate revised targets in rain-affected limited-overs matches. It considers how many overs and wickets are remaining, and calculates a 'par score' - the score the chasing team should be at to be considered equal. The method recognizes that a team with fewer overs but all wickets in hand may have a higher scoring potential than one with more overs but fewer wickets.
key_terms: Resource percentage: Measures the combined value of remaining overs and wickets
Par score: The minimum score needed to tie the match
Target: Par score + 1 for a win

powerplay.name: Powerplay Rules (T20)
powerplay.explanation: In T20 cricket, the first 6 overs of each innings are called the powerplay. During this phase, only 2 fielders are allowed outside the 30-yard circle. This restriction makes it easier for batters to score boundaries. After the powerplay, 5 fielders are allowed outside the circle.

variations.IPL: First 6 overs, max 2 fielders outside circle
variations.ODI: First 10 overs powerplay, max 2 fielders; middle 30 overs max 4; final 10 overs max 5

lbw.name: Leg Before Wicket (LBW)
lbw.explanation: A batter is out LBW if the ball would have hit the stumps but was instead intercepted by any part of the batter's body (except the hand holding the bat). For LBW to be given: (1) The ball must pitch in line with the stumps or on the off-side, (2) The impact must be in line with the stumps (unless the batter played a shot), and (3) The ball must be going on to hit the stumps.
lbw.drs_review: Under DRS (Decision Review System), ball-tracking technology (Hawk-Eye) shows where the ball pitched, where it hit the pad, and whether it would have hit the stumps. If impact is outside off-stump and no shot was played, the batter is usually not out.

super_over.name: Super Over
super_over.explanation: A tie-breaking method used in limited-overs cricket when a match ends in a tie. Each team gets one additional over (6 balls) to score as many runs as possible. The team with the higher score in the Super Over wins. Each team nominates 3 batters and 1 bowler for the Super Over. If still tied, another Super Over is played, though some tournaments have other tiebreaker rules.
super_over.history: First used in IPL 2009, now standard in most T20 leagues including IPL, Big Bash, PSL

types.wide: A wide is called when the bowler delivers the ball too far away from the batter for them to normally reach it. Awards 1 run to the batting side plus an extra ball. The batter cannot be out off a wide except stumped, run out, or hit the ball twice.
types.noball: Called for illegal bowling action (overstepped the crease, too many fielders outside circle, bowling arm issues). Awards 1 run plus an extra ball. The same batter faces the re-bowled ball.
types.bye: Runs taken when the batter does not touch the ball with bat or body, but it passes the wicketkeeper and batters run. No credit to batter's score.
types.legbye: Runs taken when the ball hits the batter's body (not the hand holding the bat) and batters run. No credit to batter's score.

drs.name: Decision Review System (DRS)
drs.explanation: A system allowing teams to challenge umpire decisions using technology. Each team gets a limited number of reviews per innings. The third umpire uses ball-tracking (Hawk-Eye), edge detection (UltraEdge), and ball-station cameras to determine if the decision should be overturned.

outcomes.reviewed_out: Decision changed to out even if original was not out
outcomes.reviewed_not_out: Decision changed to not out even if original was out

drs.lbw_criteria: For LBW reviews: (1) Ball must not be a no-ball, (2) Ball must hit in line with stumps or batter must not have played a shot, (3) Ball must be going on to hit stumps

ipl_fantasy_tips.description: General tips for Dream11 fantasy team selection

selection_strategy.context: Top-order batters in strong batting lineups
selection_strategy.reason: Higher chance of facing more balls and scoring runs
Better chance of taking wickets and bowling maidens
Can earn points from both batting and bowling
Can score catches and stumpings in addition to batting points

selection_strategy.context: Players facing spinners if pitch is turning
selection_strategy.reason: Different strategies for different pitch conditions

batting_friendly.characteristics: Flat pitch, even bounce, low seam movement
batting_friendly.strategy: Prioritize aggressive batters, all-rounders, and less bowler points

bowling_friendly.strategy: Prioritize top bowlers, wicketkeepers with catching opportunities

spin_friendly.characteristics: Dry pitch, dust, turn after 10-15 overs
spin_friendly.strategy: Prioritize spinner bowlers, batters who handle spin well
